title: Barrister Salary Australia: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a barrister salary in Australia from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week formula. Includes tax, super, and award comparisons.
salarySummary: A barrister earning $100 per hour for a 38-hour week would have an annual gross salary of $197,600 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How is a barrister salary in Australia calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. This assumes consistent hours and no unpaid overtime.

faqs.q: Does the Legal Services Award apply to barristers?
faqs.a: No. The Legal Services Award covers employees such as law clerks and legal administrative staff, not self-employed barristers. Barristers typically negotiate their own fees and are not covered by award minimum rates.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and a barrister’s typical rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $33.05 for casuals including loading. Barristers generally earn well above this, often $100–$500+ per hour depending on experience and area of law.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Barrister Salary Australia Landscape

When you search for "barrister salary australia", you are likely looking for a way to turn an hourly rate into a reliable annual figure. Unlike many salaried employees, barristers often charge by the hour or by the brief, and their income can vary significantly. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay using the standard 38-hour week, and what the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office say about minimums, averages, and obligations.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The core calculation is straightforward: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This article assumes a 38-hour week unless stated otherwise, because that is the standard ordinary hours for full-time employees under most awards and the National Employment Standards. For example, if you charge $100 per hour, your annual gross would be $100 × 38 × 52 = $197,600. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly.

It is also helpful to think in fortnights. A fortnightly gross is simply the weekly amount multiplied by 2. For a $100 hourly rate at 38 hours per week, the weekly gross is $3,800, so the fortnightly gross is $7,600. This can be useful when comparing to salary offers that are quoted fortnightly.

### Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum $33.05 per hour. However, barristers are not covered by the Legal Services Award 2020 (MA000116), which applies to employees like law clerks and legal administrative staff. The award rates for a Level 6 law clerk are $36.03 per hour, but these are minimums for employees, not self-employed barristers. Barristers typically earn far more, often $100 to $500 per hour or more, depending on seniority, location, and area of practice.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must pay 12% of ordinary earnings into a super fund for employees. For self-employed barristers, you may need to arrange your own super contributions. The maximum contribution base for the 2026–27 year is $270,830. Super is calculated on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it. For example, if your annual gross is $197,600, the super contribution (if paid by a client or employer) would be an additional $23,712, bringing total remuneration to $221,312. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the $197,600 example, the tax would be approximately $54,637 plus Medicare of $3,952, leaving an after-tax income of about $139,011. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Average Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118 annually. A barrister earning $100 per hour is well above these averages, but many barristers earn significantly more, especially in commercial law. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides broader comparisons.

### Casual Loading and Penalty Rates

If you are employed as a casual barrister (rare, but possible in some legal roles), you would receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. This is not the same as penalty rates for overtime or weekend work. The Legal Services Award specifies overtime rates for employees: 150% for the first 3 hours Monday to Saturday, 200% after that, and 250% on public holidays. Casual employees get an additional 25% on those rates. However, most barristers are not award-covered employees, so these rates are a reference point for legal support staff, not barristers themselves.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: if you are self-employed, you may need to account for GST and business expenses separately. The tool assumes a consistent 38-hour week and does not include penalty rates or allowances.

### Key Differences from Salaried Employees

A barrister salary in Australia is not a fixed annual amount. Unlike a full-time employee under an award, barristers often have irregular hours, periods without work, and additional costs such as chambers fees, insurance, and professional development. The hourly-to-annual conversion gives a rough guide, but actual income may be lower due to downtime or higher due to premium work. Always consult a tax professional for your specific situation.

For more detailed pay rates across industries, see the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) on this site.
